content.thinking:
I'm sketching the qilin's design: a deer/horse-ish body with ox hooves, a dragon head with antlers, scaled skin, a flame-like mane, and a fish or ox tail, roughly horse-sized with a shoulder height around 1.35 m. I also want to check how sample code imports things before structuring my own.

For the palette, I'm going with jade-teal scales edged in gold over a cream belly, gold antlers with glowing tips, cloud-swirl mane cards in cream/blue/pink, crimson tassel accents, and amber eyes. I'm now thinking through the skeleton structure — pelvis as root, spine chain to chest, neck to head to jaw, a tail chain, and four legs each with their own joint chain.

Now I'm working out the actual coordinates: model facing +Z, floor at y=0, deer-like proportions with slender legs, shoulder height around 1.3m, body length roughly 1.2m from chest to rump, and placing the spine joints along that centerline from hips to chest.

Then I'm mapping the neck curving up and forward into a swan-like arc, the dragon-esque snout head pointing forward-down, and antlers rising to about 2.5m total height -- sizing the qilin roughly horse-scale but a touch taller at the shoulder, around 1.3m, to feel properly mythic.

For the skeleton structure, I'll root everything at the hips joint, with the spine chain running forward to the chest, a tail chain extending backward, and a neck chain branching off the chest end -- hind legs attach at the hips, fore legs at the chest. The body skin is a loft connecting the spine and hips bones for the barrel, with the neck and tail swept separately so they overlap cleanly at the junctions.

Now I'm working out the front leg proportions for something like a deer or horse -- shoulder, elbow, knee, fetlock, and hoof joints, measuring segment lengths (upper arm, forearm, cannon) against the total distance from shoulder to hoof to get a slightly bent stance, and figuring out which direction each joint should bend (elbow back, knee forward, fetlock back) to look anatomically right.

For the hind legs, I'm setting up the hip-to-hoof chain with thigh, hock, cannon, and fetlock segments, assigning lengths that total a bit more than the straight-line distance for a natural bend, and alternating the bend directions (forward at the stifle, back at the hock, forward-ish at the fetlock) so the joint names map correctly onto the limb chain with a tip at the hoof.

Now I'm thinking through the hooves themselves—going cloven ox-style since this is a qilin, built from two small wedge/frustum halves in gold, plus adding fetlock tufts, gold ankle bands with tassels, and cloud puffs at the knee for decoration. The leg skin will be a smooth swept surface with wider shoulder radii where the body loft meets the top of the leg.

Now I'm defining the leg's radius profile along its length, then layering scale-pattern paint in jade with gold edges onto it, wrapped in cel shading, and considering how to combine that with a cream countershaded belly using a fur-edge paint nested inside the cel shader—checking that the shadow resolves correctly through the paint stack and that scale texel size stays reasonable on the texture sheet.

I'm sizing the shared paint atlas—weighing 1024 versus 2048 resolution for crisper scale edges given the painted surface area—and settling on 2048 for the draft, while keeping the flat color palette modest since paints and textures don't count against that limit. Now I'm moving on to designing the dragon-deer head: an elongated skull with a lofted snout, jaw, nostrils, and a cloud-like chin beard.

For the facial features I'm planning long rigid whiskers sweeping from the muzzle, large amber anime-style eyes, brow ridges, swept-back leaf-shaped ears with pink interiors, and deciding between antlers versus a single qilin horn—landing on paired branching antlers in gold with jade gradients plus a glowing forehead gem, since the spec calls for antlers. For construction, I'm sketching how to sprout the antlers from the head surface using curved beam sweeps with branching tines offset along the main beam's surface.

Now I'm working out the antler tines as smaller sweeps or spikes branching off curved points along the main beam, capped with small glowing octahedron gems at the tips, plus gold coronet rings at the antler base. Then I'm shifting to the cloud mane running along the neck's dorsal line, planning to build it from layered cloud-curl card textures in white, pale blue, and pink gradients, shaded by each card's facing normal for a toon-lit look.

Light actually comes from the renderer's standard material since baked cel-shading only applies to painted parts, so the cards get a flat two-tone anime style with ink outlines drawn directly into the SVG textures. For geometry, I'm placing around 14 large cloud-curl card frames along the neck line flowing backward and sideways, alongside a possible 3D version using extruded scalloped cloud-outline crests with gradient paint for a xiangyun-style mane running like a dorsal ridge.

Generating cloud outline math...

Offsetting both sides to form a polygon merged with the blob arc risks self-intersection, so I'm considering a sweep-based approach instead, extruding a flat curve with a cross-section for the mane and tail shapes.

Actually simpler: I'll build the mane from flat cloud-wisp cards drawn in 2D plus flattened low-poly spheres for volume, using 3-4 pastel texture variants at ~0.35m scale, with matching cloud tufts at the shins, fetlocks, and tail tip, and simple scalloped extruded blobs for the body. I'm also weighing whether to add flame details since qilin sometimes have fire motifs on the body.

For the tail, I'm planning an ox/lion-style long tail with a fan-shaped cloud tuft at the tip, using wispy cards from t=0.5 to 1 for the plume. I'm tallying joint budget: 20 for legs, 4 spine, 4 neck, a few for head/jaw/ears, 6 tail, maybe 2 antler joints, and 8 for whisker chains—keeping well under the 160 cap. For the whiskers, I'm considering using the "tentacle" role for flowing dragon-style whisker chains of 4 joints each, since allowed roles are hinge, tail, or tentacle.

Now I'm working out the ears as leaf-shaped extrusions with a hinge joint per ear, and the jaw as a separate lower-jaw piece with fang cones and a tongue, plus an upper jaw with its own fangs for the dragon snout. For the head frame, I'm deciding to use model-space offsets rather than head-local axes, defining a helper that computes points as forward/up/right offsets from the head joint's position so I can place snout and jaw geometry predictably.

Since the head is tilted with a downward pitch, I'm reconsidering and instead setting up a rotated region using a quaternion that tips the forward axis downward by rotating about X, so head-attached parts naturally follow the snout's tilt instead of using raw world axes.

Defining head geometry coordinates...

Still defining loft stations...

For the nose I'm adding nostril spheres and a nose pad, and for the eyes I'm placing an amber decal onto the skull surface around the cranium/brow area, sized roughly 0.07×0.095 relative to the ~0.55 head length.

Now I'm layering on facial features: swept gold brow flicks with dragon crest spikes, jade/gold cheek frills extruded along the jaw, a hanging cloud-style chin beard, whiskers, a glowing gem on the forehead, and horns rooted behind the brow. I'm shaping the neck taper from 0.17 at the base down to 0.1 near the head with joints neck1 through neck4, then starting the body loft stations, defining width/height profiles at the rump and hips.

I'm figuring out torso proportions across stations—belly, chest, and breast widths and heights—checking how the withers height and shoulder attachment points relate to leg placement so the legs sit mostly inside the body with a slight shoulder bump, then moving on to hoof height.

Now I'm working out the leg-to-hoof transition: the limb target should land near the top of the hoof (~0.075), with cloven hoof geometry extending from the ground up to that point, and the floor resting at y≈0. I'm also planning a color gradient down the lower legs toward gold "socks" using the shared coat palette.

For paint logic I want a hard cel-style boundary separating lower-leg color from body color based on height, with a jagged tooth edge running along the leg's circumference in the x-z plane rather than a straight line. I'm also considering adding gold greave-like bands near the knee by cutting loop sections into the leg surface after the sweep.

Loop cuts on the leg surface can mark joint positions like the fetlock, with the cutting plane oriented along the bone's axis, which is useful for banding and for adding feathering details -- rings of cards flowing downward like tufts, or small cloud-puff clusters at the fetlock. I'm also thinking about adding a row of small ridge details along the dorsal line for extra texture beyond the painted scales.

Along the spine I want gold or jade fin-like plates following the body's centerline, plus decal motifs on the flanks -- a swirling golden cloud scroll design rendered in SVG for an auspicious touch. For ornamentation, I'm planning a gold chest piece with a glowing jade gem, along with ribbon sashes flowing from the shoulders in crimson and gold, built as chained joints so they trail dramatically down the body.

I'm also thinking about small cloud wisps near the hooves for visual flair, while keeping the model grounded and staying within budget for parts and triangle count. Now I'm sketching out the actual joint and chain hierarchy in code, starting from the hips as the root and building a spine chain through catmull-rom control points up toward the chest.

Writing skeleton code...

Checking proportions against body length of 1.4 — the neck reads slightly long but that suits a stylized, elegant anime look. Total height from poll to antler tips lands around 2.55, which feels appropriate for a tall mythic qilin-horse-deer creature at roughly 2.5 meters.

Now I'm working out the tail curve, deciding between a hanging ox-like tail with a flame tuft versus a flowing, lifted horse-flag style — I'll go with a rising, curling arc that clears the floor comfortably, with a tuft covering the end.

I'm setting up the body loft, parenting the tail start point to the hips joint and defining the bone chain (hips, spine) that the loft path will follow, with rump stations near the hips owned by that joint. Now I'm defining the loft station widths and heights along this path.

Defining the neck taper...

Adding haunch bulge with larger radius at the hip to suggest muscle, then setting up the hind leg root and target positions for the geometry.

Checking the hind leg's four-segment chain against the distance between hip and foot target to make sure the bend angles look natural with the hock curving back. Now setting up the foreleg root and target positions similarly.

Side naming resolves left/right by sign, then I'm sketching the cloven hoof geometry as two wedge halves built from cone/cylinder shapes at the hoof joint position.

Skipping dewclaws for now, adding fetlock tufts and a gold cuff band with a cloud puff instead. Moving to antlers — planning the root position behind the brow on the cranium, then mapping out a branched beam path sweeping up, back, and forward to the tips, accounting for how the head's 24° downward pitch tilts the region's local axes away from true world-up.

Rather than fight the tilted region coordinates, I'll switch to plain model-space for the antlers: setting the base near the skull top and plotting catmull-rom control points that curve the beam upward and backward before arcing toward the tip.

Writing antler sweep geometry...

Placing gold torus rings around the beam base, then working out antler coloring with a gradient from gold base to pale ivory tips using nested cel paints.

For the ears, I'm sketching a leaf-shaped outline extruded outward and back from the side of the head, figuring out which axis the outline's width and length should run along so it sits naturally against the skull.

I'm angling the ear axis up and outward like a deer's, leaning it back slightly while keeping it roughly perpendicular to the thickness direction, and planning two layered extrudes per ear — an outer jade/cream shape and a smaller inner pink one set slightly forward for the inner-ear detail.

Now I'm mapping out the whiskers: for each side, a chain of points flows from the muzzle outward and backward into a long sweeping curve about a meter in length, tapering from a thin radius down to almost nothing, built as a joint chain of four bones parented to the head and colored pale gold/cream. I'm deciding to give each side one long whisker plus a shorter secondary one rather than cluttering with more.

For the mane, I'm building a dorsal sweep of frames along the neck using a sweep function, then generating cloud-like cards along those frames with flowing orientation back and down, bending smoothly with the neck joints, and spreading cards laterally at angles roughly ±35-40° from center for volume.

I realize default flow-back cards would appear edge-on from the side view, so I need to vary flow direction per card with alternating lateral components so the cards face outward enough to read as thick fur from the side rather than thin edges.

For volume, I'm also adding 3D cumulus-style blobs along the dorsal mane line using small icosahedron clusters, grouped in lumps of three at each station, shaded from white at the base to a lavender-pink tip for a soft cloud-like mane texture.

Picking colors for the puffs — pearly white as the lit tone with bluish-lavender shadow, plus pink and sky-blue variants scattered across the lumps. I'm placing these clouds along the neck, chest tufts, tail root, elbow/knee puffs, and hoof clouds using a helper function that builds 3-5 spheres per cluster, keeping triangle counts manageable even with thousands of lumps. Now I'm starting on the gold ornaments, beginning with a lathed chest plate/gorget at the base of the neck.

Still designing ornaments...

I'll skip detailed back scales beyond paint but add small raised gold crest plates. For the eyes, I'm placing a decal near the skull region using a nearest-point hit on the skin surface, then orienting the decal's direction outward and forward so the eye reads correctly despite the head's pitch.

Since this is meant to look anime-style with large front-facing eyes rather than horse-like side eyes, I'll angle them around 50° azimuth and size them roughly 0.07×0.1 relative to a cranium radius of 0.1, keeping the cranium wide enough that the eyes don't overwhelm the face. I also want to add ink brow strokes within the eye texture for extra character.

Next I'm planning the smaller facial features: dark teal nostril spheres at the snout tip, maybe flared like a dragon's, tiny fang cones at the upper jaw and a small lower tusk, and I'll skip the tongue or keep it minimal. For the resting pose I'm considering a slight jaw gap of about 4° with an ink line suggesting a faint smile, though this detail isn't critical. Then I move on to the chest ornament and mane before settling on a jade color palette, likely a teal-green that gradients toward deeper blue near the top.

Still writing color palette...

Writing leg fur and scale logic...

For the lower jaw and mane I'm keeping the cream coloring consistent. For eyes I'm leaning toward an amber-gold iris to contrast against the jade coat. For glow elements I'm planning the forehead gem, antler tip crystals, and chest gem each with their own glowing colors, plus considering a glowing emblem decal on the flanks as a swirled gold-white motif.

Now I'm sketching out the SVG cloud wisp card designs with tapering curl shapes in a few color variants.

Still writing spiral path...

Working out shading passes with offset highlightWorking out the exact spiral geometry for the wisp's centerline...

Continuing the spiral math, setting the center at (44,46) so the stem connects smoothly upward, then working out the decreasing radius per loop and tapering thickness to mimic a xiangyun cloud shape with a bulbous head and thin tail.

Now I'm planning the other decorative cards: a fetlock/tail tuft reusing the wisp shapes with different tinting, a chest tassel ornament with a gold knot and red strands, and a flank emblem using a gold "ruyi" double-spiral scroll motif around 0.34m across. I'm also thinking through how to divide the mane into separate parts/cards for rendering.

Each card counts as a distinct texture-tint combination, with colour variants handled through SVG parameters for a modest total quad count. Now I'm sketching the sash ribbons flowing from the shoulders and neck, defining the path points so they drape along the flank and flutter out behind the figure.

I'll keep ribbons flat and horizontal with widths along world X, letting paths undulate in Y with slight outward spread in X for a trailing sash effect, and color them crimson with gold edge bands along the width.

I'll paint gold crisscross stripes along the ribbon using a modulo pattern on the t-coordinate, keeping accents sparse so the model doesn't feel cluttered. For the tail, I'll scale jade with gold bands and add tuft cards near the tip using a ring placed along the tail's curve.

Now I'm setting up the file's imports—THREE, the builder and frame utilities, math and path helpers, limb IK, paint/texture modules, and the toon/glow kits—making sure I only pull in what's actually used so nothing triggers unused-import errors.

Defining color palette...

Now I'm setting up the builder config and starting the skeleton, defining the hips joint as the root spine joint.

Building spine chain segments...

Adding ears, whiskers, and antler joints attached to the head, then starting to define the head region with its anchor point.

Working out the cranium sphere placement in the tilted head region, positioning it slightly forward and using the region's baked orientation quaternion for the bone attachment.

I'm also mapping out the snout as a loft shape, defining a series of cross-section stations moving forward along the tilted head axis with progressively narrower widths and heights to taper toward the nose.

For the lower jaw, I'm positioning it below the snout as its own loft, adjusting the y-coordinates so its top surface meets the snout's bottom edge where the mouth closes, ensuring the jaw doesn't clip through the upper snout geometry.

I'm adding small gold whisker-root bumps near the muzzle sides, a gold-jade brow ridge sweeping from the forehead to the snout with optional flame-tuft spikes, and planning a cheek frill as an extruded fin shape.

Writing extrusion outline coordinates...

Computing the perpendicular thickness direction via cross product, then skipping the jade scale spikes idea and moving to positioning eye decals on the cranium sphere's surface.

I'm using the nearest-point lookup to find the hit location on the skin, then thinking through whether the decal projection target should include both the cranium and snout surfaces so the eye grid doesn't miss near the boundary edge, and placing the eyes roughly where the loft meets the cranium.

Checking eye size ratios against the kit's constraints, confirming the up-vector default and the mirror flag logic for left vs right eyes matching the kit example, then sketching placement for fangs, skipping the tongue and mouth line for now, and considering a forehead gem near where the snout's top curve begins.

Now I'm placing a crimson-glowing diamond gem tilted above the brow with a gold crest plate beneath it, adding a cloud tuft forelock between the antlers and flowing wisp cards over the brow, plus a hanging chin-beard tuft -- working out which bone (jaw vs head) each frame should attach to since unlisted points default to the nearest joint.

Now I'm defining five hanging beard cards attached to the jaw bone with a backward-forward sway, then plotting whisker chains per side as curved paths that sweep outward from the muzzle, dip and curl backward in a long swirl trailing past the body, naming each chain so they auto-generate symmetric left/right versions.

Adding whisker joints with gold cel-shaded tube radius tapering toward the tips, plus tiny glowing pearl orbs rigged to the last joint of each whisker for a magical shimmer. I'm also sketching a second, shorter whisker pair lower on the jaw, and defining the ear's leaf-shaped outline with a sharp pointed tip for extrusion into a 3D ear mesh aimed outward from the head.

Working out ear orientation vectors...

I'm deciding which ear surface should carry the pink inner coloring relative to the outward-facing normal, since that's the side visible from the front-3/4 viewing angle typical of deer anatomy.

Now I'm working out the antler base position by rotating the head-relative offset by the 22° head pitch, computing the resulting world coordinates numerically to anchor where the antlers attach.

From there I'm laying out the antler path as a sequence of points offset from that base, curving outward and upward with forward-sweeping tines, bringing the total model height to around 2.7-2.75m overall for the qilin.

Working out tine placement along the beam...

Still planning antler coloring...

For cloud puffs I'm defining a function that builds lumpy icosahedron clusters attached to joints, considering whether flat faceted normals or smooth normals read better with cel shading for that anime look.

Actually smooth sphere normals make more sense here for a clean terminator curve, so I'll switch to SphereGeometry with modest segment counts since it's indexed and gives naturally smooth shading. Now I'm figuring out how to distribute mane lumps along the neck's dorsal curve using the along-path helper.

I realize b.stick is better for lumps since it seats a sphere along the frame's facing axis, sinking by an embed fraction of its height, and the frame carries bone info so it rides the skin properly. Lateral offsets can be done using the frame's own local axes via at.moved, shifting sideways while still carrying the bone attachment.

Now I'm planning rows of cloud lumps along the dorsal angles, roughly three rows at ±48° and 0°, each with about eight positions, giving a modest triangle budget. I'm also thinking through wisp cards radiating from the dorsal frames and side flank cards sweeping backward at the neck, plus varying the cloud shading between lit white and lavender shadow tones with pink/sky color variants for visual interest.

Then I turn to clustering lumps at the chest, elbows, knees, fetlocks, and tail tip, adding mirrored flank emblem decals with a glowing swirl pattern for symmetry, and sketching out small gold shoulder ornament plates to sit atop the cloud shapes.

I'm planning the gold accessories now—a neck collar with a gem, a chest pendant, leg bands at the forearms and hind cannons, and gold hoof caps—starting with the collar as a swept loop following the neck's curve using a tangent-facing frame.

Next I'm positioning a jade pendant at the front of the collar near the chest base, with an octahedron gem in a gold bezel and three hanging tassels, finding its placement by locating the nearest point on the body surface. Then I'm adding a row of dorsal blades running along the top of the body using a repeated stick function at intervals along the loft.

I'm sketching out further decoration ideas - scale plates on shoulders, belly tassels, cloud-shaped lumps at the hips and haunches, glowing ruyi decals, tapering jade scales along the tail with a flame-tuft tip, cloven gold hooves with pastern caps, and gold bands looped around the leg cannons positioned using the chain's tangent frame at roughly 70% along each leg.

Now I'm tuning the leg sweep radii, tapering front legs from a thick shoulder down through elbow, forearm, knee, cannon, fetlock, to a slimmer pastern for an elegant deer-like proportion, while hind legs get a bulkier thigh radius that bulges past the body's half-width before tapering similarly. The hoof geometry attaches to the leg chain's tip joint, and I'm starting to define the fur/paint texture for the legs using a gold edge pattern based on position.

Writing scale and fur pattern definitions...

Estimating total painted surface area across body, legs, neck, and head at roughly 8 m², I'm working out texel density needed for a 2048² texture, landing around 1.6mm per texel—so a scale size of 0.075 would span roughly 45 texels.

For textures, I'm planning a 2048 paint sheet with an atlas sized up to 4096, and deciding on four mane wisp variants (white, pink, sky, gold-cream) as 256px SVGs, with tail and fetlock tufts reusing those cards with flow variations. Writing wisp generation function...

Adjusting the spiral position and widths...

For rendering, I need outlines to union properly: draw all ink-colored circles first for the outline, then layer the fill circles on top, then add a shading pass with lighter circles offset toward the upper-left to simulate directional light.

For the tail and fetlock, I'll reuse the flame-wisp function at a smaller scale, and I'm planning a separate tassel SVG with its own viewBox and a gold knot decoration at the top.

For the hanging card, since it drapes with the root edge upward, I realize the tassel needs to be drawn upside-down: knot at the bottom where it attaches, strands and skirt extending toward the top of the drawing. Then for the emblem, I'm sketching a gold swirl design in a 100x100 viewBox with stroke widths scaled so they render crisply at 256px output size.

Now I'm drawing a ruyi cloud scroll shape as two joined spirals with outer arcs and small accent dots, keeping the gold strokes simple since they're meant to sit as glowing decals on jade. I'm also starting a rough part-count tally for the skeleton-bound pieces -- body, neck, leg sweeps, and so on -- to estimate total asset complexity.

Writing leg builder logic...

Defining chain joint paths...

Checking the shoulder position is close to the body edge but still within bounds given the ellipse offset. I'm confirming the parent joints for fore and hind legs trace back correctly to spine and hip roots, then setting up the sweep call to skin the fore leg chain and defining the hoof joint from the leg tip.

Writing hoof box code...

For color, I'm thinking deep indigo-purple hooves with a gold cap sock above for contrast, splitting each hoof into two halves with a small cleft gap between them.

Now I'm working out fetlock tufts as cloud wisps—rings of cards placed around the fetlock joint, facing outward and tilted to lean downward along the bone direction, with the flow vector flattened so cards point down and to the side.

For the ring helper, I want it to accept a count, radius, angle range, and tilt, returning the joints and the generated items.

For knee and elbow puffs, I'm thinking of placing small sphere clusters at each joint—three per leg—offset from the joint's local position to form rounded lumps, attached to the joint bone so they move naturally with the leg.

Actually, I'm reconsidering—cloud puffs feel more appropriate for the qilin's mane than scattered at every joint, so I'll skip knee and elbow lumps and reserve that cloud texture for fetlocks and shoulders instead. I'm now shifting to planning the tail chain with its own sweep, cards, and lumps, then moving to a "cloud bib" cluster of lumps across the chest, using surface point lookups on the body mesh so they inherit the correct skin weights for deformation.

Now I'm working out how the dorsal neck cards should be angled and flow, defining lateral and backward flow vectors for side rows versus an alternating pattern for the center row, and reasoning through how card orientation works—since a card's face follows its flow direction, lateral-outward flow means those cards will read as face-on when viewed from the side.

Then I'm planning counts for the frames and sparse back wisps, adding a gem helper function for small octahedron accents with glow, and starting to sketch out the antler-building logic that generates joint positions along each side using small vector offsets.

Still writing antler geometry...

Adding forelockI'm placing forelock lumps between the antlers with cards flowing forward-down, anchored near the head bone since literal frames default to the nearest joint. Skipping the mouth upturn, tongue, and lower lip details, I'm focusing on the snout painting and whisker tip pearls before moving to the ribbon chain geometry, positioning ribbon points along a descending curve on either side of the tail.

For the ribbon start point, I'm adjusting the y-coordinate so it emerges naturally from beneath the neck/collar area like a draped scarf rather than floating above the body, then setting up the chain with catmull interpolation parented to the spine joint.

For the ribbon's shape, I'm sweeping a tapering box section that widens slightly toward the end, planning a flared diagonal cut at the tip with a gold tassel ornament attached to the final chain point. I still need to work out the tail definition and head decals for the eyes.

Now I'm figuring out the surface API for combining nested part arrays like cranium and snout, and confirming that loft/sweep calls return chainable objects with `.at` access for positioning cloud-like lumps near the neck. I'm also tallying flat color counts to stay under the 64-color limit, planning to rely mostly on cel-shaded paints and reserving flats for ink, gems, teeth, pearl, nostril, and eye details.

Setting up imports and metadata for the Qilin creature file...

Writing SVG texture code...

Plotting the spiral coordinates for the stem and curl shape, checking that the two segments connect smoothly at the transition point...

Drawing the layered circles for each bead using ink outline, base shade, lit highlight, and bright spot colors, then starting on the tassel SVG that hangs below.

Good, that orientation checks out — knot at top when hanging, skirt widening downward as drawn. Now I'm defining the eye parameters with iris color and glow styling.

Writing color palettes for jade scales, cream scales, and the coat...

Still defining leg and limb textures...

I'm setting up the ribbon pChecking the neck taper against the cranium radius confirms a good match, and I'm working out how the head attaches at the neck's top end relative to the cranium's center position.

Applying the rotation transform to the cranium center point, I get it placed at roughly (0, 1.893, 1.109), which lines up well with the neck end at (0, 1.94, 1.02) — the neck pokes into the back-top of the cranium as intended, with the rounded cap giving some extra margin. Now I'm thinking about placing mane lumps along the dorsal side of the neck sweep.

Moving to the head features, I'm setting up a helper to convert local coordinates to world points, then working out eye placement relative to the cranium ellipsoid and snout dimensions — checking that the cranium's cross-sectional width at the eye's z-depth is wide enough to fit the eye socket position.

I'll handle the eye decal's projection direction angled for a 3/4 view, which risks gaps but should work in practice, then move on to tongue, teeth, and small cheek fur tuft cards flaring back from the jaw sides.

For the cheek tufts, I'm orienting each card sideways and flowing backward along the cheek using a frame built from the bone position. Then I'm adding gold/jade spike details on the brow using a spike helper that takes a base point, direction, length, and radius, followed by setting up the ear joint hinge and extruding the ear geometry from its base.

I'm defining typed outline arrays for the ear shapes, positioning the inner ear slightly offset from the outer ear along the normal so it sits proud by a small margin, and double-checking the normal direction logic holds up. Then I'm setting up texture arrays for wisp effects, a seeded RNG, and dorsal loop frames, making sure the Frame type import matches what's actually exported from the frame module.

Now I'm working through the mane generation, looping along the neck spline to build frames at various angles and parameters, confirming how the `along` helper's callback behaves so I collect the right frame data for lump placement.

Writing lump placement function...

Still writing tail geometry...

Adding tail-tip fur ring and chest lumps, then moving to dorsal gold blade cones along the body with elongated square-pyramid geometry for a blade-like look. I want to finalize everything and run a typecheck once it's all written.

Now I'm adding jade gems to the collar and working out the flank decal placement on the body mesh, figuring out orientation so the emblem faces correctly when viewed from the side, with mirroring for the opposite flank and a glow effect applied to the decal.

Time to write the file, then run typecheck, preview with box, and take a shot to view the result.

input.command: ls; ls samples scratch 2>/dev/null | head; grep -n "export" src/frame.ts | head -20
